note: Art this project did not generate. Every other PNG beside this file is rendered by
tools/sprites and re-rendered pixel for pixel by `npm run sprites:check`; a key declared
here is the exception, and declaring it is what makes it an exception rather than a file
nobody noticed. The owner's call of 2026-09-09 (docs/30, 'Art we did not generate') was
that sprites are commissioned to this project's own spec rather than bought as a pack, so
an authored key is held to the same canvas, the same anchor and the same published bounds
as the rig it stands beside -- `npm run godot:check:authored` is where that is mechanical.
The owner's call of 2026-09-17 (docs/30, 'The outpost pack, adopted') was the opposite for
a second batch: `godot/art/simplyzombies/` is a hand-made pack and it is adopted whole,
overwriting the generated art it replaces.
Read by two things, which is the whole point of it being a file rather than a list in code:
tools/sprites/build.py (so --check knows not to try to regenerate it) and
presentation/appearance.gd's `canvas_of` (so the renderer knows its shape). The two-copies
arrangement every other shape table in this project carries -- PAWN_KEYS in Python and in
GDScript, VEHICLE_FOOTPRINTS in both -- is what this replaces for authored art.
An entry may declare `source`: `{path, crop?, pad?}`, `path` relative to godot/ (the same
string as after res://). tools/sprites/build.py reproduces it -- crop, then pad, never
repainted or resized, godot/art/simplyzombies/STYLE.md's own rule for its mechanical steps
-- so `--check` holds a sourced key to decoded pixels the same way it holds a generated one,
and `python3 tools/sprites/build.py` can write it. A key with no `source` (every
commissioned one so far) keeps the existence-and-shape check only: nothing here can
reproduce a PNG an artist delivered by hand.
An entry may instead be a **family**: `members` names several keys that each carry their
own `source` and share the family's `canvas`. The family key itself is not a file -- it is
the one `reads` and `kind` are declared against, for art that is one declaration but many
pictures (a walk cycle's frames, a garment's four sides). `godot:check:authored`'s READS
lane judges a family by its family key; a member is never content-named on its own.
`kind` decides which bounds the gate holds a key to:
rig      a body. The published bounds in README.md: height, head, shoulders, clearance,
soles on the bottom row. The eight generated rigs are held to the same numbers
by the same lane, so the spec cannot drift from the art that already meets it.
overlay  a piece of equipment composited onto a body. WORN_LOOK_OK owns its fit.
tile     a tile-sized picture seen from above, centred on its ground point.
pack_rig / pack_overlay / module / sheet / prop
placeholders for the outpost pack's later slices -- bodies that turn and walk,
worn gear, wall modules, animated effect sheets, and prop pictures generally.
MANIFEST accepts them today; no shape lane judges one yet, and each gains one
when the slice that reads it lands (docs/23's 'Art & renderer -- the outpost
pack' group).
`reads` names what draws it -- a content id whose appearance block declares the key. Art
nothing reads is the dead-socket shape this project has paid for twelve times, so the gate
refuses a key that names nothing rather than letting it sit here looking finished. Since
2026-09-17 `reads` only has to be ONE of the content ids that declare the key, not the last
one loaded -- two bases sharing one icon are both allowed to claim it.
Optional `anchor: [x, y]` (pixels) and `palette: "generator"|"pack"` are accepted by
MANIFEST for later slices to read; nothing draws from either yet.
